an0949.user: Need a sober read on something. Post-iOS, my two dashboards have completely diverged and I can't reconcile them. Meta's ads manager is reporting 4.3 ROAS on ₹6L spend last 30 days. Shopify, last-click, says 1.6 on the same spend. That's not a rounding gap, that's two different universes. Which one do I actually trust to make budget decisions?
an0949.assistant:
Neither, as an absolute. That's the non-obvious part — you're not trying to find the 'real' number, you're refereeing two systems that are structurally incapable of agreeing.

Meta's 4.3 is modelled conversions on a 7-day-click (and view-through) window — it claims credit generously and fills attribution gaps with statistical modelling post-iOS. Shopify last-click is the opposite bias: it only credits the final touch, so it hands your branded-search and direct traffic the win and starves Meta of any assist it actually earned. The truth genuinely sits between 1.6 and 4.3. You will burn weeks trying to make them match and they never will.

So stop managing to platform ROAS at all. Anchor on blended CAC: total spend across everything ÷ actual new customers Shopify recorded that month. ₹6L ÷ your real new-customer count is a single, honest number that doesn't care which dashboard is lying. Manage budget to that, and to contribution per new customer, not to a ROAS that two tools will argue about forever.

Caveat: blended CAC blurs which channel drove what, so once it's stable, layer in a periodic geo-lift or a spend-down test on Meta to see what actually moves total orders. That's your tiebreaker — incrementality, not dashboard arbitration.

an0950.user: My Google Performance Max CTR is only 1.4% and I think that's why sales are soft. Last 30 days I got 21,000 visits, 1,794 add to carts, 1,093 reached checkout, and 220 purchases. I feel like the ads just aren't pulling enough clicks. How do I fix the CTR?
an0950.assistant:
CTR isn't your problem — 1.4% on Pmax is normal, and your traffic is doing its job. Look at where the money is actually leaking, because it's nowhere near the ad.

Walk the funnel: 1,794 add-to-carts on 21,000 visits is 8.5% ATC — that's healthy intent, your acquisition is fine. 1,093 of those reach checkout. But only 220 buy. That's a 20% checkout→purchase rate. A working checkout converts 50–70% of people who reached it. You're losing four out of five people standing at the till with their wallet out.

That is not a targeting or creative issue. It's friction at the very last step: surprise shipping cost revealed late, a forced account-creation wall, or missing UPI/COD options Indian buyers expect. If you'd pushed CTR up you'd just have funnelled more people into the same broken checkout.

The one move: instrument the checkout and watch session recordings of the drop-off. Recover even half of that gap — from 20% to ~40% — and purchases roughly double on the exact same spend. Your ad money is fine; leave it alone.

Caveat: confirm those 220 are de-duped real orders and not counting failed/abandoned payment attempts, so you're chasing the true gap.

an0952.user: My CAC on Performance Max is ₹442 and I keep trying everything to bring it down. AOV is ₹850, ROAS sits at 1.9, CTR 1.7%. Margin is 24%. The ads just feel expensive. How do I lower my CAC?
an0952.assistant:
You're trying to fix the ads. The ads aren't what's broken — your margin is, and lowering CAC won't save a unit that's underwater before the ad even runs.

Do the contribution math: ₹850 × 24% − ₹442 = ₹204 − ₹442 = −₹238 per order. Every sale loses you ₹238 on the gross. Even if you were a genius and cut CAC by ₹100, you'd still be at −₹138 — still bleeding. There is no targeting tweak, no creative, no bid strategy that fixes a 24% gross margin. The ad account is a costume; the disease is the P&L.

The mechanism: a 24% gross margin in D2C nutrition means COGS plus packaging plus shipping is eating three-quarters of every order before a single rupee touches marketing. You can't acquire your way out of that.

So stop optimising CAC and go fix the margin: renegotiate COGS, raise price, or lift AOV through bundles/subscriptions so the order can actually carry a ₹442 acquisition cost. To even break even at ₹442 CAC and ₹850 AOV, you'd need ~52% gross margin. That's the target, not a lower CPC.

Caveat: if 24% is contribution after some costs rather than true gross margin, tell me which — it changes how far you have to move. But the order of operations doesn't change: margin first.

What would count as real: the same direction for 3–4 consecutive weeks, or a single move big enough to obviously clear the noise — think 25–30%+, not 11%. Until you see that, you don't have a problem, you have a normal week.
